newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Cheung Kong to book HK$7.7 bln extra gain.
newsitem.headline: Cheung Kong to book HK$7.7 bln extra gain.

text.p: Cheung Kong (Holdings) Ltd said on Wednesday a HK$7.7 billion gain from its group restructuring will be booked in 1997 or beyond, with most of that expected to be recognised this year.
"We booked HK$1.5 billion as an exceptional item (gain) from the restructuring (in 1996)," deputy chairman Victor Li told a news conference. "And HK$7.7 billion has yet to be booked."

That added up to a total HK$9.2 billion gain from the group restructuring, which included the transfer of the company's stake in Cheung Kong Infrastructure Holdings Ltd (CKI) to Hutchison Whampoa Ltd and the 1996 flotation of CKI.
Last month, Cheung Kong said the estimated surplus on the transfer of its CKI stake to Hutchison and the CKI flotation amounted to HK$9.63 billion.
Hutchison is an associate of Cheung Kong.
Cheung Kong chairman Li Ka-shing attributed the discrepancy between HK$9.2 billion and HK$9.63 billion to taxation reasons. He did not elaborate.
The group booked a 1996 exceptional gain of HK$1.51 billion from the dilution of the group's interest through a placement and new issue of shares in CKI.
The chairman, who also chairs Hutchison, said the latter will book in 1997 an exceptional gain of HK$1.2 billion from Cheung Kong group's restructuring.

Last month, Hutchison said it would book an exceptional proift of HK$1.24 billion from the disposal of its stake in Hongkong Electric Holdings Ltd to CKI. But then it did not say when that profit would be booked.
